survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a governance country note describing institutional responsibilities for Lithuania’s adult skills system; it does not analyze student-level assessment microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, analytic subsample, or complex survey weighting scheme. No plausible values (PV) or achievement scaling procedures are applied because there is no assessment scoring model estimated here. As a result, there are no student or replicate weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT, BRR/JRR) to apply. For any future empirical analysis using adult-skills assessment microdata, analysts should use the official ILSA/OECD/IEA weight variables provided with the dataset to account for stratification and clustering, but such guidance is not operationalized in this note.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this is a descriptive policy/governance note and does not estimate or model cognitive achievement outcomes from an ILSA-style assessment with PV-based scoring. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical model fit to microdata with item nonresponse or missing covariates; the note compiles governance responsibilities and expenditure structure from secondary sources. Therefore, PV and missing-data procedures are outside the scope of this document’s methodology.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used secondary information to describe Lithuania’s adult skills governance structure; no student-level assessment dataset was analyzed and no analytic subsample was constructed.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides a qualitative overview of how Lithuania’s adult skills system is governed, focusing on the division of responsibilities across national government and 60 municipalities. It reports the overall governance and expenditure structure, including the share of general government expenditure at the subnational level (22.7%), and summarizes which institutions are responsible for strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, and delivery across policy areas (VET, HE, CET, AE, and ALMP). The note includes governance “allocation of responsibilities” tables and an infographic mapping stakeholders and reporting lines. Because it does not use ILSA-style student assessment microdata, it does not involve assessment scaling, plausible values, sampling weights, or predictive modeling. Consequently, there are no model performance metrics or benchmark achievement results; the “findings” are institutional and policy-structure descriptions intended to inform governance and coordination discussions.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the document is a governance/policy description rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis. It contains no student sample, no assessment domain scoring, and no statistical or ML modeling pipeline, so fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not meaningfully defined. The absence of these elements reflects the document’s purpose as a descriptive OECD country note compiled from secondary sources.
